rows.subtopic: HCF and LCM by Prime Factorisation
rows.stem: There are two sections A and B of Grade X. There are 28 students in Section A and 30 students in Section B. What is the minimum number of books you will acquire for the class library so that they can be distributed equally among students of Section A or Section B ?
rows.solution:
The number of books must divide equally among 28 students and also among 30 students, so it must be a common multiple of 28 and 30. The minimum such number is their LCM.

\(28 = 2^2 \times 7\) and \(30 = 2 \times 3 \times 5\), so \(\text{LCM} = 2^2 \times 3 \times 5 \times 7 = 420\).

The minimum number of books is 420, which is option (C) \(420\).

rows.chapter: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
rows.subtopic: Consistency from the Ratios of Coefficients
rows.stem: The pair of linear equations \(\dfrac{3x}{2} + \dfrac{5y}{3} = 7\) and \(9x + 10y = 14\), is :
rows.solution:
Multiplying the first equation by 6 gives \(9x + 10y = 42\). The second equation is \(9x + 10y = 14\).

In ratio form: \(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} = \dfrac{3/2}{9} = \dfrac{1}{6}\), \(\dfrac{b_1}{b_2} = \dfrac{5/3}{10} = \dfrac{1}{6}\) and \(\dfrac{c_1}{c_2} = \dfrac{7}{14} = \dfrac{1}{2}\).

So \(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} = \dfrac{b_1}{b_2} \ne \dfrac{c_1}{c_2}\): the lines are parallel and have no common solution. The pair is inconsistent, which is option (B) inconsistent.

rows.stem: The value of x for which \(2x\), \((x + 10)\) and \((3x + 2)\) are the three consecutive terms of an A.P. is :
rows.solution:
For three consecutive terms of an A.P., twice the middle term equals the sum of the other two:

\(2(x + 10) = 2x + (3x + 2)\), so \(2x + 20 = 5x + 2\), giving \(3x = 18\) and \(x = 6\).

Check: the terms are 12, 16, 20, with common difference 4. The value is 6, which is option (A) \(6\).

rows.stem: If the distance between the points \((4, p)\) and \((1, 0)\) is 5, then p is equal to :
rows.solution:
By the distance formula, \(\sqrt{(4 - 1)^2 + (p - 0)^2} = 5\), so \(9 + p^2 = 25\).

\(p^2 = 16\), so \(p = 4\) or \(p = -4\); both points \((4, 4)\) and \((4, -4)\) are 5 units from \((1, 0)\). This is option (A) \(\pm 4\).

rows.subtopic: Zeroes and Coefficients of a Quadratic Polynomial
rows.stem: Find the value of p, for which one zero of the quadratic polynomial \(px^2 - 14x + 8\) is 6 times the other.
rows.solution:
Let the zeroes be \(\alpha\) and \(6\alpha\).

Sum of the zeroes: \(\alpha + 6\alpha = \dfrac{14}{p}\), so \(7\alpha = \dfrac{14}{p}\) and \(\alpha = \dfrac{2}{p}\).

Product of the zeroes: \(\alpha \times 6\alpha = \dfrac{8}{p}\), so \(6\left(\dfrac{2}{p}\right)^2 = \dfrac{8}{p}\), that is \(\dfrac{24}{p^2} = \dfrac{8}{p}\).

Since \(p \ne 0\), this gives \(24 = 8p\) and \(p = 3\). (Check: \(3x^2 - 14x + 8 = (3x - 2)(x - 4)\), with zeroes \(\dfrac{2}{3}\) and 4, and \(4 = 6 \times \dfrac{2}{3}\).)

rows.stem: Find the area of the segment AYB shown in the figure, if the radius of the circle is 21 cm and \(\angle AOB = 120^\circ\). [Use \(\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}\)]
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - circle with centre O, radii OA and OB of 21 cm with the 120 degree angle AOB marked, chord AB, and the minor segment AYB shaded with Y on the minor arc; that AYB is the MINOR segment is shown only in the drawing. Page idx 18.
rows.solution:
Area of segment AYB = area of sector OAYB \(-\) area of triangle AOB.

Area of the sector \(= \dfrac{120}{360} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 21 \times 21 = 462\ \text{cm}^2\).

For the triangle, draw \(OM \perp AB\). Since \(OA = OB\), OM bisects \(\angle AOB\), so \(\angle AOM = 60^\circ\). Then \(OM = 21\cos 60^\circ = \dfrac{21}{2}\) cm and \(AM = 21\sin 60^\circ = \dfrac{21\sqrt{3}}{2}\) cm, so \(AB = 21\sqrt{3}\) cm.

Area of triangle AOB \(= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 21\sqrt{3} \times \dfrac{21}{2} = \dfrac{441\sqrt{3}}{4}\ \text{cm}^2\).

Area of segment AYB \(= \left(462 - \dfrac{441\sqrt{3}}{4}\right)\ \text{cm}^2 = \dfrac{21}{4}\left(88 - 21\sqrt{3}\right)\ \text{cm}^2\), about \(271{\cdot}04\ \text{cm}^2\).

rows.stem: Prove that the tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact.
rows.solution:
Given: a circle with centre O and a tangent XY touching it at P. To prove: \(OP \perp XY\).

Proof: take any point Q on XY other than P, and join OQ.

A tangent meets the circle at exactly one point, so Q lies outside the circle. So OQ is longer than the radius: \(OQ > OP\).

This holds for every point of XY except P, so OP is the shortest of all the segments from O to the line XY.

The shortest segment from a point to a line is the perpendicular to it. So \(OP \perp XY\): the tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact.

rows.subtopic: Number of Tangents from an External Point
rows.stem: If a regular hexagon ABCDEF circumscribes a circle, then prove that AB + CD + EF = BC + DE + FA.
rows.solution:
Let the circle touch AB, BC, CD, DE, EF and FA at P, Q, R, S, T and U respectively.

The lengths of the tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal, so

\(AP = AU\), \(BP = BQ\), \(CQ = CR\), \(DR = DS\), \(ES = ET\), \(FT = FU\).

\(AB + CD + EF = (AP + PB) + (CR + RD) + (ET + TF)\)

\(= AU + BQ + CQ + DS + ES + FU\)

\(= (BQ + QC) + (DS + SE) + (FU + UA) = BC + DE + FA\).

So \(AB + CD + EF = BC + DE + FA\). (The argument uses only the equal tangents, so it holds for any hexagon that circumscribes a circle, not just a regular one.)

rows.stem:
If the median of the following distribution is \(32{\cdot}5\), then find the values of x and y.

rows.subtopic: Solving a Quadratic Equation by Factorisation
rows.stem: In a flight of 600 km, an aircraft slowed down its speed due to bad weather. Its average speed for the trip reduced by 200 km/h from its usual speed and time of flight increased by 30 minutes. Find the scheduled duration of the flight.
rows.solution:
Let the usual speed of the aircraft be x km/h. The usual time for 600 km is \(\dfrac{600}{x}\) hours, and at the reduced speed \((x - 200)\) km/h it is \(\dfrac{600}{x - 200}\) hours.

The time increased by 30 minutes, that is \(\dfrac{1}{2}\) hour:

\(\dfrac{600}{x - 200} - \dfrac{600}{x} = \dfrac{1}{2}\), so \(\dfrac{600 \times 200}{x(x - 200)} = \dfrac{1}{2}\) and \(x(x - 200) = 240000\).

\(x^2 - 200x - 240000 = 0\), that is \((x - 600)(x + 400) = 0\), so \(x = 600\) (a speed cannot be negative).

The scheduled duration of the flight is \(\dfrac{600}{600} = 1\) hour.

rows.subtopic: Solving a Quadratic Equation by Factorisation
rows.stem: Two pipes are used to fill a swimming pool. If the pipe of the larger diameter is used for 4 hours and the pipe of the smaller diameter for 9 hours, only half of the pool can be filled. Find how long it would take for each pipe to fill the pool, separately, if the pipe of smaller diameter takes 10 hours more than the pipe of larger diameter to fill the pool.
rows.solution:
Let the pipe of larger diameter fill the pool alone in x hours. Then the pipe of smaller diameter takes \((x + 10)\) hours.

In one hour they fill \(\dfrac{1}{x}\) and \(\dfrac{1}{x + 10}\) of the pool. Using them for 4 hours and 9 hours fills half the pool:

\(\dfrac{4}{x} + \dfrac{9}{x + 10} = \dfrac{1}{2}\), so \(2[4(x + 10) + 9x] = x(x + 10)\), that is \(26x + 80 = x^2 + 10x\).

\(x^2 - 16x - 80 = 0\), that is \((x - 20)(x + 4) = 0\), so \(x = 20\) (a time cannot be negative).

The pipe of larger diameter takes 20 hours and the pipe of smaller diameter takes 30 hours to fill the pool. (Check: \(\dfrac{4}{20} + \dfrac{9}{30} = \dfrac{1}{5} + \dfrac{3}{10} = \dfrac{1}{2}\).)
